items.title: Woman killed, sister and motorcyclist seriously injured after lorry hits their stalled car in Nilai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A woman was killed while her sister and a motorcyclist were seriously injured after a lorry crashed into their broken-down car at Kilometre 284.4 of the North-South Expressway northbound near Nilai this morning. Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said the district traffic complaints counter received information about the accident from the Nilai district police operations room at 9.01am. Johari said a 22-year-old man riding a Honda RS 150 arrived at the scene and tried to help the woman move the vehicle.

items.title: Philippines ex-leader Duterte makes first appearance at ICC
items.summary: THE HAGUE: Former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte appeared in person at the International Criminal Court for the first time Wednesday, as he faces charges over his "war on drugs" that killed thousands. The 81-year-old had appeared by videolink when he was first brought to the court in The Hague, but had since skipped various hearings, with his defence team claiming he was too ill. Judge Joanna Korner noted his appearance in court for the first time, and said he could leave the court at any time without seeking permission from the bench.

items.title: Cable thieves caught on video in Jalan Jelatek, RM15,000 in losses reported
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are investigating an attempted cable theft in Jalan Jelatek, Datuk Keramat, which allegedly caused losses estimated at RM15,000. Ampang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said a report was lodged after a company representative received a video of the incident at 4.30pm yesterday. Khairul Anuar said police had also detected the video circulating on Threads.

items.title: Cabinet ministers call for unity, respect on Malaysia Day
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Malaysia Day served as a reminder that the country was built on mutual understanding, unity and a shared determination to move forward together. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Malaysia's peace and harmony stemmed from the sacrifices of previous generations and the sustained efforts of all Malaysians. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said being Malaysian was not merely an identity but a shared responsibility to safeguard peace, preserve harmony and defend the country's sovereignty.

items.title: AI ambition needs smarter computing, not just more power
items.summary: LETTER: The current excitement around artificial intelligence can create the impression that more computing power automatically produces better innovation. Responsible AI therefore includes knowing when not to use the largest AI system available. Good computing should also be efficient.

items.title: Anwar condemns drone threat near Makkah, urges restraint
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has condemned the reported drone threat near Makkah, saying any attempt to endanger the safety and sanctity of Islam's holiest city is unacceptable. Anwar said Malaysia appreciated the swift action taken by Saudi Arabia to protect residents and pilgrims in Makkah. Earlier, Saudi Arabia issued emergency alerts warning of a "potential danger" in Jeddah, Makkah and Taif, urging residents to seek shelter and follow official safety instructions, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

items.title: English village votes to 'secede' from UK over asylum centre plan
items.summary: LONDON: An English village of around 350 people announced Wednesday that a vast majority of residents had voted yes in an "independence referendum" staged to protest plans to house over 1,200 migrants in a nearby facility. The village's parish council announced that with 312 ballots counted, 285 had voted to secede from Britain over plans to house asylum seekers in a nearby disused military site, in a symbolic vote with no recognised legal basis. The local parish council chair Tim McNally said that the village will now be known as the "principality of Piddington."

items.title: Anwar calls for shared progress on Malaysia Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said no region or community should be left behind in the country's development. He said Malaysia Day should serve as a renewed commitment to national unity and shared progress. "Happy Malaysia Day!"

items.title: Wife attack: Man with 27 criminal, drug offence cases arrested
items.summary: Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the unemployed man, in his late 20s, was detained at the compound of the Dang Wangi district police headquarters on Sept 8. "Acting on information, a team from the Cheras district police Criminal Investigation Division (D7) arrested the local man at the compound of the Dang Wangi district police headquarters on Sept 8," Fadil said in a statement today. The suspect's previous records comprised 15 criminal cases and 12 offences under the Dangerous Drugs Act.

items.title: China opens major canal linking landlocked regions to sea
items.summary: BEIJING: China opened a major canal on Wednesday that will provide landlocked areas with direct access to the sea, state media said, reducing transport times and costs as the country aims to bolster trade ties with regional neighbours. The 134-kilometre Pinglu Canal took four years to build and links Nanning, in the southern manufacturing region of Guangxi, to the Gulf of Tonkin, flanked by China and Vietnam. Goods from southwestern China previously had to be transported to the southern metropolis of Guangzhou in order to reach the sea, but the new canal will cut the journey by more than 560 kilometres, state news agency Xinhua said.

items.title: Policeman injured chasing cable theft suspects in Kluang
items.summary: Kluang deputy police chief Superintendent Nik Mohd Azmi Husin said police received a report at 5.45am that a motorcycle patrol officer had been injured and immediately rushed to the scene. "The district police headquarters confirmed receiving a report that the patrol officer was injured after falling while pursuing suspects believed to be involved in cable theft, as seen in a video that went viral on social media. "Investigations found that the cable theft occurred at 1.57am, with the suspects using a Mitsubishi four-wheel-drive vehicle to tow the cables," he said.

items.title: Johari backs DRB-HICOM, Proton push into India's auto sector
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani has backed DRB-HICOM Bhd and Proton Holdings Bhd's efforts to explore opportunities in India's automotive industry. This includes the potential use of the group's Tanjung Malim manufacturing capabilities in Perak to supply components or establish partnerships with Indian automotive players. Johari said DRB-HICOM was exploring ways to leverage its manufacturing and automotive capabilities in Malaysia to participate directly in India.

items.title: A-G: Muhyiddin still faces three Jana Wibawa charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar has stressed that the three charges against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin linked to the Jana Wibawa programme are still being pursued in court. Dusuki said the decision not to proceed with four charges against Muhyiddin involved Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and was unrelated to the Jana Wibawa charges. The Bukhary Equity case has nothing to do with Jana Wibawa.

items.title: Malaysia among economies positioned to capture upside as Asean growth paths diverge
items.summary: This is amid stronger investment flows, industrial expansion and technology adoption reshaping the region's growth outlook. The report, "From Tailwinds to Trade-Offs: Southeast Asia Outlook 2026-2035", projects Southeast Asia's six largest economies - Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam - to grow by an average of 4.8 per cent annually between 2026 and 2035. While the regional growth outlook remains broadly intact, the report said economic trajectories are diverging.

items.title: Anwar: Losing mother in prison was 'most painful' moment
items.summary: Anwar said being behind bars and unable to do anything as his beloved mother took her final breath was an immense ordeal. Recalling the episode, Anwar said he was informed about his mother's deteriorating condition by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail. "Losing a mother is much more difficult than losing a father.

items.title: 129 still missing four days after capsize of ship in Indonesia's Java Sea
items.summary: BANJARMASIN: Desperation and frustration are growing among families of the 129 people still missing following the weekend capsizing of a ship in Indonesia's Java Sea, as persistent heavy seas and bad weather continue to restrict search-and-rescue operations. The Virgo Transport 8 was carrying 243 people on a 20-hour voyage from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan when it capsized in bad weather early on Sunday. On Wednesday, the official death toll stood at six people with 108 rescued and 129 unaccounted for, tallies that have not changed since Sunday.

items.title: Malaysia-Australia defence ties set for deeper strategic cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia-Australia defence ties are set to deepen following Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin's working visit to Australia, with both sides looking to pursue more strategic, substantive and outcome-oriented cooperation. He will then travel to Geelong for a courtesy call and bilateral meeting with Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles. Khaled said the meeting, following last year's gathering in Kuala Lumpur, would assess progress in defence cooperation, explore new opportunities and chart the future direction of bilateral defence ties.

items.title: Malaysia prioritises diplomacy over compensation in addressing transboundary haze, says Zahid
items.summary: KUCHING: Malaysia prioritises long-term diplomatic cooperation and early preventive measures over seeking compensation from neighbouring countries in addressing transboundary haze. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also the National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said a prudent and structured diplomatic approach is the most effective way to address sensitive issues among Asean member states while ensuring optimal technical coordination. Also present were Sarawak Deputy Premier and Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, and deputy Rural and Regional Development minister Datuk Rubiah Wang.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar to invite Myanmar president, push for Rohingya repatriation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will invite Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing to make an official visit to Malaysia as part of efforts to expedite the repatriation of Rohingya refugees. Anwar said the move was aimed at finding a long-term solution to the issue, which has increasingly sparked concern among locals. We can accept Myanmar, but they must take back the refugees.

items.title: Malaysia to seek preventive measures, diplomatic cooperation over transboundary haze, says Zahid
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 16 — Malaysia prioritises long-term diplomatic cooperation and early preventive measures over seeking compensation from neighbouring countries in addressing the issue of transboundary haze, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee Chairman, said a prudent and structured diplomatic approach is the most effective way to address sensitive issues among Asean member states while ensuring optimal technical coordination. Also present were Sarawak Deputy Premier and Chairman of the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN), Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, and Deputy Minister of Rural and Regional Development, Datuk Rubiah Wang.

items.title: Anwar to review impact of electricity bill increase at special meeting tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A special meeting will be held tomorrow with the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), the Energy Commission (EC), Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and the Ministry of Finance (MoF). The meeting will review immediate mitigation measures to reduce the impact of the electricity bill increase on affected households. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that upon his return from India and the Maldives, his attention remained focused on the people’s concerns regarding the recent increase in electricity bills.

items.title: 'Young Curators' turns museums into classrooms for 2,373 students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rather than simply viewing artefacts behind glass, 2,373 students were given the chance to step into the shoes of curators through the 'Bermalam di Muzium' (Night at the Museum) 2026 programme. Themed 'Young Curators', the programme was held at 32 museums nationwide to encourage young people to learn about, appreciate and preserve the country's heritage. Also present were Museums Department (JMM) deputy director-general (Policy) Mohamad Shawali Badi, JMM deputy director-general (Museums) Mohd Razaimi Hamat, Akademi Kenegaraan Malaysia (AKM) deputy director-general (Management) Saliza Mokhtar, and National Museum director Zamrul Amri Zakaria.

items.title: Policeman injured while chasing 4WD involved in Kluang cable theft case
items.summary: Kluang deputy police chief Superintendent Nik Mohd Azmi Husin said the incident is believed to have occurred at 5.54am when two policemen on motorcycles were chasing a Mitsubishi vehicle. He said the suspect, believed to be involved in an earlier cable theft incident, had an uncut cable at the rear of the vehicle. Nik Mohd Azmi was responding to a video posted on Threads showing two policemen chasing a red Mitsubishi pick-up truck in Kluang town.

items.title: Smuggled cigarettes hidden beneath concrete piles seized at Tuas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An attempt to smuggle 4,500 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes into Singapore using a Malaysia-registered trailer was foiled after the contraband was found hidden beneath a load of concrete piles. "Further inspection uncovered 4,500 cartons of duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden beneath the load of concrete piles. ICA said the driver and seized cigarettes were subsequently handed over to Singapore Customs for further investigation.

items.title: Bersatu still has strength despite member exits, says Youth chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu remains relevant and retains influence through its representatives in Parliament and state assemblies despite defections by grassroots members, says Bersatu Youth chief Muhammad Hilman Idham. He said the party, led by former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, would contest the upcoming Melaka election. However, whether Bersatu will contest independently or cooperate with another coalition is expected to be announced by Muhyiddin on Saturday.

items.title: Stray elephant safely relocated from Terengganu to Royal Belum State Park
items.summary: HULU TERENGGANU: A male elephant that had wandered into Kampung Kolam, Ajil, here, last week was safely relocated to Royal Belum State Park this morning. Terengganu Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) director Dennis Ten Choon Yung said the wild elephant was captured last Thursday before being relocated today. He said the operation began at 9am and involved 24 personnel from Terengganu Perhilitan and the National Elephant Conservation Centre (PKGK) in Kuala Gandah.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar calls urgent meeting tomorrow to address higher electricity bills [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will hold a special meeting tomorrow to examine immediate measures to ease the impact of rising electricity bills on affected households. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the meeting would involve the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry, Energy Commission, Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and Finance Ministry. Anwar said the government remained committed to targeted subsidies to ensure most domestic consumers remained protected.

items.title: Every Malaysian has a role in defending country, says Khaled
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Every Malaysian has a role to play in defending the country, including by safeguarding unity and resisting elements that seek to divide society. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said national defence was not solely the responsibility of the military, as citizens also had a role to play. "Today, we not only celebrate Malaysia Day, but also commemorate another important day for the country – the 93rd Armed Forces Day.

items.title: Anwar: 'Prime ministers come and go, but country must be saved'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has appealed to Malaysians to give his administration more time to pursue reforms, acknowledging public impatience over the pace of change while warning that faster action could trigger greater political resistance. Addressing those who feel his administration's progress has fallen short of expectations, Anwar acknowledged his shortcomings but said his Cabinet was pushing ahead with reforms despite difficult circumstances. Anwar said accelerating reforms risked provoking intense resistance from entrenched interests seeking to preserve the status quo.

items.title: Three houses destroyed in Alor Star fire
items.summary: ALOR STAR: Three houses along Jalan Stadium here were destroyed in a fire last night. The Kedah Fire and Rescue Department operations centre received an emergency call regarding the incident at 9.40pm. "Upon arrival, the operations commander reported that the fire involved three houses, comprising two Class B two-storey houses and one Class C single-storey house.

items.title: Chinese investors rush into US stocks as Beijing opens wider path overseas
items.summary: SHANGHAI: Chinese investors are piling into foreign assets, especially US stock funds, after regulators lifted outbound quotas, unlocking pent-up demand as domestic yields are at rock bottom and Beijing tightens unofficial routes for moving money abroad. Late last month China's foreign exchange regulator raised the outstanding Qualified Domestic Institutional Investor quota by US$6.8 billion to a record US$183 billion. "There remains huge appetite in China for US tech stocks."

items.title: Malaysians in Jeddah and Makkah safe following Saudi emergency alert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians in Jeddah and Makkah are safe following an emergency alert issued by Saudi Arabian authorities yesterday. Malaysian Consul-General in Jeddah Tengku Mohd Dzaraif Raja Abdul Kadir said the consulate had distributed the official graphic issued by the Saudi Arabian Ministry of Interior to WhatsApp groups for Malaysians in the Hijazi region. "We distributed the graphic from the Saudi Interior Ministry to WhatsApp groups for Malaysians in the Hijazi region.

items.title: Malaysia-China relations continue to flourish, expand into emerging sectors
items.summary: BEIJING: Malaysia-China relations continue to flourish, with both countries committed to strengthening cooperation in trade, investment, technology and other high-potential areas, said Malaysia's Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad. "The relationship between Malaysia and China, which is based on mutual respect and trust, continues to grow from strength to strength," he said in his remarks at the Malaysia National Day Reception held at the China World Hotel. Norman said China had remained Malaysia's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching US$132.50 billion (RM541.90 billion) in 2025, accounting for 17.7 per cent of Malaysia's total global trade.

items.title: 200,000 residents oppose 17,000-unit Bukit Jalil apartment project
items.summary: BUKIT JALIL: More than 200,000 residents from three housing areas here are opposing the proposed construction of 17,000 apartment units, citing concerns over worsening congestion and inadequate infrastructure. Protest committee chairman Zainuddin Zainal said the opposition involved residents of Bukit Jalil, Bandar Kinrara and Taman Puncak Jalil. He said residents were unanimously opposed to the high-density development, which they feared would worsen congestion in the area.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan DOE ramps up enforcement as haze hits unhealthy levels
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 16 — The Negeri Sembilan Department of Environment (DOE) is stepping up ground-level monitoring, particularly on open burning activities, following worsening haze conditions in several districts in the state. State DOE director Abdul Aziz Parmin said other sources being closely monitored included factories, quarries, motor vehicles, development projects, land clearing and any activities that could contribute to dust emissions and cause air pollution. He said all actions related to the haze situation would be referred to the National Haze Action Plan, while at the state level, the department would continuously update the State Disaster Management Committee on the situation.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: My views on Najib’s pardon given honestly
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 —Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she had expressed her views on former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon application during the Pardons Board meeting on Sept 11, after reviewing the written opinion of the Attorney General. The statement was issued in response to remarks by Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said regarding the deferment of Najib’s pardon application. Hannah said she had expressed her views in her capacity as the minister responsible for the Federal Territories.

items.title: Schools advised to stagger students seeking medical checks, says Perak health exco
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 16 — The Perak government has advised schools to coordinate with District Health Offices and relevant health facilities before bringing large numbers of students for medical examinations following an outbreak. The advice came after a boarding school in Ipoh brought 57 students with Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) to a nearby health clinic simultaneously, despite being advised to bring them in stages. Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said bringing symptomatic students in stages would help prevent congestion at health facilities and reduce the risk of infection transmission.

items.title: Guan Eng: Umno no longer brings value to Penang government amid cooperation with Perikatan, PAS
items.summary: Lim said Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow appeared more focused on criticising him than addressing Umno’s recent attacks on PH, creating what he described as an impression that Chow feared Umno might quit the state government. “Instead of hitting back at Umno for working with the opposition PN, Chow chose to criticise me,” Lim said, adding that Penang PH leaders should not be afraid of offending “an extremist Umno” that he claimed had indulged in divisive rhetoric against non-Muslim minorities and shown little inclusivity toward non-Malays. Even without Umno’s two assemblymen, Lim said, PH would still command a two‑thirds majority in the Penang legislative assembly.

items.title: Perak exco: 46 students at Influenza A cluster school suffer flu-like illness
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 16 — Forty-six students at a boarding school in Ipoh have been diagnosed with influenza-like illness (ILI) following an Influenza A cluster detected at the school, Perak Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman A. Sivanesan said. He said the cases were identified after health officials screened and assessed 61 students with symptoms up to Sept 14, while 14 others were found to have upper respiratory tract infections and one had conjunctivitis. According to him, the school had first brought 57 symptomatic students to a nearby health clinic on Monday, before the figure rose to 61 when an additional 39 symptomatic students were brought in yesterday.

items.title: Raja Muda of Selangor, MACC chief commissioner discuss anti-corruption initiatives
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — Efforts to strengthen the fight against corruption were among the matters discussed by Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman. The MACC said the matter was discussed when Tengku Amir Shah granted an audience to Abd Halim at Istana Selangor, Bukit Kiara, last Monday. In a statement today, the commission said Tengku Amir Shah was also briefed on its latest developments and ongoing initiatives, particularly those relating to anti-corruption efforts in Selangor.

items.title: Sanusi: Too early for seat talks as Kedah PAS, Umno explore political cooperation
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 16 — Kedah PAS and Umno are focusing on creating a positive environment for further discussions on political cooperation, with no requests yet made over seat allocations, Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor reportedly said. The Umno delegation was led by Kedah Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Mahdzir Khalid and Alor Setar Umno division chief and former Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ahmad Bashah Md Hanipah. PAS was represented by Kedah commissioner and PAS Central Ulama Council chief Datuk Ahmad Yahya, deputy commissioner II Dr Ahmad Fakhruddin Sheikh Fakhrurazi and Kedah secretary Senator Musoddaq Ahmad.

items.title: Penang air quality hits unhealthy levels statewide, Minden records API of 167
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 16 — Air quality at all four monitoring stations in Penang reached unhealthy levels as of 11am today, with Minden recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 167. State Housing and Environment Committee chairman Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said Balik Pulau recorded an API reading of 164, followed by Seberang Jaya at 162 and Seberang Perai at 160. He said Minden and Balik Pulau had registered unhealthy readings over the past 24 hours, while readings in Seberang Jaya and Seberang Perai had risen from moderate to unhealthy levels.

items.title: Police: Sri Petaling bomb scare turns out to be team-building game equipment left behind by worker
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A suspicious plastic box found unattended in front of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Sri Petaling earlier today contained toy building blocks belonging to a company that organises training and team-building programmes, police said today. Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said police were contacted by a company director, who informed them that the unattended plastic box belonged to his company. “Investigations found that the box had been left behind by a company employee and contained 20 plastic toy blocks from a game called ‘Radioactive Bomb’, which are used as equipment for group team-building activities.

items.title: MA63 still binding, no ‘new deal’ needed, says Armizan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 16 — The Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) did not cease to exist upon the enactment of the Federal Constitution but remains in force, with the commitments and responsibilities contained therein continuing to be relevant and binding on all parties, said Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. “This term reaffirms the commitment and responsibility of all parties that agreed to sign the agreement to form the Federation of Malaysia,” he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with Malaysia Day today. Armizan said Malaysia, which was formed in 1963, has now reached 63 years, although Sept 16 only became an important date in the official national calendar and was officially celebrated as Malaysia Day from 2010.

items.title: KLIA standardises e-hailing entry fees at RM2 across both terminals effective today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has standardised the entry fee for e-hailing vehicles at RM2, inclusive of tax, across Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, effective today. Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) in a statement here said the revised fee also represents a reduction from the previous charges of RM3 at Terminal 1 and RM2.16 at Terminal 2, providing passengers with a single, consistent rate for e-hailing pick-ups at both terminals. Meanwhile, Senior General Manager for Passenger Experience at KLIA Abd Hasman Abd Muhimin said the continued enhancements to KLIA’s e-hailing facilities reflect the airport operator’s commitment to improving the overall passenger journey while ensuring that airport operations remain orderly, efficient and responsive to evolving needs.

items.title: Fahmi says Sarawak redelineation has begun but gives no election deadline (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 16 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil made no commitment on whether the electoral boundary review would be completed before the next Sarawak election, but stressed that the process had already begun. Fahmi highlighted the commitment by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the EC to expedite the redelineation process. Meanwhile, EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said in a statement on Sept 13 that the commission would carry out the review of electoral boundaries subject to amendments to the Federal Constitution.

items.title: Home Ministry vows to crush foreign worker fraud syndicates ‘at the root’
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — The Home Ministry (KDN) is determined to dismantle the operations of syndicates manipulating the foreign worker system and falsifying documents at the root, without any tolerance, said its Minister, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the Immigration Department (JIM) was no longer taking a defensive approach, but was instead acting aggressively to cripple the syndicates at their source. Saifuddin Nasution said the fake e-PLKS were sold for RM150 each, while the fake police reports were sold for RM70 each.

items.title: Haze flips west: 41 areas in Peninsular Malaysia hit unhealthy levels as Sabah, Sarawak clear
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A total of 41 areas in Peninsular Malaysia recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 9 am today. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy readings, namely Johan Setia (187), Shah Alam (175), Petaling Jaya (169), Klang (167), Banting (166) and Kuala Selangor (164). In Penang, four areas recorded unhealthy readings, namely Minden (166), Balik Pulau (164), Seberang Jaya (162) and Seberang Perai (160).

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of heavy rain and strong winds across Penang, Sabah and Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds affecting several areas in Sarawak and Sabah until 11am today, as well as the whole of Penang until noon. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected areas in Sarawak are Limbang, Miri (Miri and Subis), and Kuching (Lundu and Kuching). In Sabah, the warning covers the West Coast areas of Penampang, Putatan, Papar, Tuaran, Ranau and Kota Kinabalu, as well as the Interior areas of Membakut, Beaufort, Kuala Penyu, Tambunan, Keningau and Tenom.

items.title: Malaysia Day: Selangor Sultan urges Malaysians to strengthen unity, cherish peace
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 16 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has called on Malaysians to continue strengthening unity and appreciate the peace and harmony enjoyed by the country in conjunction with the Malaysia Day celebration today. “Happy Malaysia Day, Malaysia!” said His Royal Highness.

items.title: Nearly nine in 10 intimate-partner murders in Malaysia since 2017 were unplanned, police say
items.summary: Of the intimate-partner cases, 99 involved married couples, eight involved former husbands killing their former wives and 58 involved boyfriends and girlfriends. Among the 21 killings where police found evidence of prior planning, six involved husbands killing their wives, two involved wives killing their husbands and four involved former husbands killing their former wives. Of the 144 cases without prior planning, 76 involved husbands killing their wives, 15 involved wives killing their husbands, four involved former husbands killing their former wives, 42 involved boyfriends killing their girlfriends and seven involved girlfriends killing their boyfriends.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh wants KL to compete with Singapore as regional concert hub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Kuala Lumpur should compete with Singapore for major international concerts rather than have Malaysian fans cross the border to watch their favourite acts, Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said, according to The Straits Times (ST). Why should my people in Kuala Lumpur go to Singapore to watch concerts and not here? The comments come as Malaysia seeks to position Kuala Lumpur as a bigger player in Southeast Asia’s live entertainment market, with the government lowering regulatory and cost barriers for international acts.

items.title: Malaysia loses US$775m a year to illicit tobacco trade as market share hits 55pc, study finds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia is estimated to be losing around US$775 million (RM3.2 billion) in tax revenue annually to illicit tobacco, with illegal products accounting for more than half of the market, according to a new regional study. According to CME, the estimated revenue lost to illicit tobacco in both Malaysia and Pakistan now exceeds the amount governments collect from tobacco taxation, suggesting significant erosion of the legal tax base. That translates to nearly US$48 in estimated revenue lost for every US$100 collected in tobacco taxes.

items.title: National interests must transcend racial, religious differences, says Aaron
items.summary: National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said that in conjunction with the 63rd Malaysia Day celebration, the people are also urged to continue respecting one another, sharing common values, and preserving the unity and harmony that are the foundations of the country’s peace, stability and prosperity. From Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah and Sarawak, each community contributes to Malaysia’s unique and rich face. “Happy Malaysia Day 2026.

items.title: Wan Junaidi calls for mature, inclusive Malaysia as nation marks Malaysia Day
items.summary: The Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak, Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, said the strength of a nation is not measured solely by economic progress or physical development, but also depends on maturity and wisdom in managing its diversity. “Malaysia today is entering an era that demands new ways of thinking. Wan Junaidi said Malaysia Day also served as a reminder that true progress could only be achieved when no one was left behind in the nation’s development.

items.title: Putrajaya Immigration detains 173 foreign nationals at Sepang construction site
items.summary: Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 88 officers of various ranks were deployed to conduct inspections at the site. He said 261 individuals, comprising 217 foreign nationals and 44 locals, were checked during the operation. Of the total, he said 147 were Bangladeshi men, 17 Indonesian nationals and nine Pakistani nationals.

items.title: More than 2.6 million Malaysians visited Indonesia in 2025 as neighbours gear up for 70 years of diplomatic ties
items.summary: Malaysia’s Chargé d’Affaires to Indonesia Farzamie Sarkawi said this at the Malaysia Day celebration hosted by the Embassy of Malaysia in Jakarta, here on Tuesday night, highlighting the unique relationship between the two countries, which share history, language, and culture. Farzamie said bilateral cooperation continues to gain momentum, with trade reaching US$34.22 billion (US$1=RM4.08) in 2025, while Malaysia remained Indonesia’s fourth-largest investor with investments amounting to US$4.5 billion. He said people-to-people connections also remained strong, with more than 2.63 million Malaysian tourists visiting Indonesia last year, making Malaysia the largest source of foreign visitors to the republic, while 4.26 million Indonesian tourists visited Malaysia.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia won’t be transit point for shipments supporting Israel’s military, suspicious cargo will be inspected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday reaffirmed Malaysia’s firm stance against allowing the country to be used as a transit point for any cargo contributing to Israel’s military operations. In a statement posted on his X account, Anwar stressed that Malaysia remains committed to preventing the country from being used to support military aggression or acts against innocent lives. “Malaysia’s position is clear and unequivocal.

items.title: Anwar calls for Malaysia-Maldives ties to deliver tangible gains in trade, tourism and digital economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia and the Maldives have ample scope to strengthen parliamentary cooperation, including through exchange visits, sharing of experiences and the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) platform, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. During the visit, he also held several meetings with the Maldives leadership to expand cooperation in strategic areas, including education, defence, trade, investment, tourism, the halal industry and the digital economy. Anwar said his meeting with Maldives Vice-President Hussain Mohamed Latheef also discussed efforts to expand cooperation in higher education, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), professional training and human capital development.

items.title: King and Queen extend Malaysia Day greetings, pray for lasting peace and unity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Their Majesties Sultan Ibrahim and Raja Zarith Sofiah, King and Queen of Malaysia, have extended Malaysia Day greetings to all Malaysians. In a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page, the King and Queen also prayed that Malaysia would continue to be blessed by Allah SWT, enjoy lasting peace, and remain protected from all forms of adversity. Sultan Ibrahim also expressed gratitude for the longstanding unity and harmony among Malaysians of different races, saying these are vital to the country’s strength and stability.
